clue.text: Cheat and attract disrespect

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
to tempt is to attract or entice

explanation.surface: Someone who cheats and lures others ends up held in low regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn or a lack of respect, a direct synonym for disrespect.

clue.text: Heart broken by composer with no a love for obesity

indicators.note: the heart word is split open so that another piece can sit inside it

parts.note: the core of something is its heart

indicators.note: the composer's name has a letter taken away, the one standing for love

parts.note: Francis Poulenc was a French composer
love is a zero score in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A composer's heart is broken, and without love he turns to food for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken by' looks like damage to the heart; it means the heart word is split open to hold the trimmed composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulence is fatness or stoutness of body, the same condition as obesity.

clue.text: Make cardinal upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cardinal number is a counting number such as ten

explanation.surface: An instruction to annoy a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but here it means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: To net a sum is to make it as profit, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Romans for instance, with energy building, running around street

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the building word runs around the street abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building

explanation.surface: The Romans, it seems, keep building with great energy and running round the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romans' is not the ancient people but Paul's Epistle to the Romans in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans is one of the New Testament letters, so it is an example of an epistle.

clue.text: Extraordinarily chummy, embracing female before warning

indicators.note: the friendly word wraps its arms around the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: pally means friendly, chummy

indicators.note: the female word comes ahead of the warning word

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
an omen is a warning sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: Someone is unusually friendly, hugging a woman before giving her a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: PALLY opens after P to hold HENOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenally means to a remarkable degree, the same as extraordinarily.

clue.text: Service provided in mountainous area.

parts.note: Mass is a church service
provided, as in on condition that, means if

explanation.surface: A church service is held up in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provided' looks like a verb meaning supplied; here it means on condition that.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a mountainous area.

clue.text: Say nothing about escort followed by senior person with interest

indicators.note: the senior word comes after the first group
the hush word goes around the escort word

parts.note: SH is a call to say nothing, be quiet
to take someone somewhere is to escort them
older means senior

explanation.surface: An older man stays quiet about the escort he hired.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeholder is a person with an interest or share in an enterprise.

clue.text: What must be round end of pipe?

parts.note: round as in plump means fat

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a pipe's end has to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a shape for the pipe end, but means plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate is what is destined to happen, whatever must be.

clue.text: Advance on army mostly lacking vigour

parts.note: re means on or concerning
the TA is the Territorial Army

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: inert means lacking vigour or sluggish

explanation.surface: Moving forward on a tired army that has run out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' is not a forward move but money paid ahead; the TA is Britain's reserve force, the Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a fee paid in advance to secure someone's services.

clue.text: Shocked husband in story returning before time

indicators.note: the story group comes ahead of the time letter
the husband letter sits inside the turned story word
the story word goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: A husband shocked by a story that comes back before its time.
explanation.walkthrough: SAGA reversed is AGAS, and H goes inside it to make AGHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock.

clue.text: Superior technique of head of government dividing union as he exercised power

indicators.note: the leader's initials split the scrambled letters into two parts
the letters are worked over and rearranged, like muscles being exercised

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
the PM, Prime Minister, heads the British government

explanation.surface: A leader splits the union while in power, showing superior skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a political story, but 'exercised' is the anagram signal and the Prime Minister's initials do the dividing.
explanation.definitionFit: One-upmanship is the art of staying a step ahead of others, a technique for seeming superior.

clue.text: Riveting not strong enough to hold post in lower position

indicators.note: the weak word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: unable means not capable, not strong enough
to post something is to put it somewhere
down means in a lower position

explanation.surface: Someone too weak to hold a post in a lower rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An unputdownable book is so riveting that you cannot stop reading.

clue.text: Mean, cheap stuff exists around old and new estates

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

indicators.note: the exists word goes around the old and new letters

parts.note: is means exists

explanation.surface: Mean, tacky goods surround the old and new estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective, stingy, but is the verb intend.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantations are large estates where crops are grown.

clue.text: Get round woman with diamonds — ecstasy follows

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman wearing diamonds, high on ecstasy, gets around the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade a rule is to get round it, escaping it by a trick.

clue.text: Coaches ousted car in snarl-up

indicators.note: a snarl-up is a tangle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Coaches thrown out as a car is caught in a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaches' looks like buses in a traffic jam; it means teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Educators are teachers, people who coach others.

clue.text: Material in cell unfamiliar to calm spy

indicators.note: unfamiliar suggests the letters are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: A calm spy confronts something strange in his prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests a prison for the spy; it is a biological cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cytoplasm is the material within a living cell outside the nucleus.

clue.text: Fixed up rail to protect minute flower

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round and protect the minute letter
fixed as in repaired or rigged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rail is repaired to shelter a tiny flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed up' reads as one phrase meaning repaired; 'Fixed' alone is the anagram signal and 'up' is part of its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula is a genus of flowering plants that includes the primrose.

clue.text: Help with work around platforms

indicators.note: around means the joined words turn round, read in reverse

parts.note: aid means help
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone helping with work all round the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia is the plural of podium, a raised platform.

clue.text: Fear produced around valley by soil testing process

indicators.note: the fear word is set around the other pieces

parts.note: terror is great fear

indicators.note: by means next to, so the soil word sits beside the valley word

parts.note: a ria is a drowned river valley
land means soil or ground

explanation.surface: Fear grips a valley next to the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: TERROR splits after T to take RIALAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial and error is a way of testing by repeated attempts until one works.

clue.text: Part of song about sun god

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
Horus is the Egyptian sky and sun god

explanation.surface: Part of a song is about the sun god.
explanation.definitionFit: The chorus is the refrain that recurs between verses of a song.

clue.text: Hard knock received by camera component brought about fragments

indicators.note: the hard and knock letters go inside the camera part
brought about means turned round, read in reverse

parts.note: a lens is part of a camera
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a rap is a knock

explanation.surface: A hard knock to the camera lens has caused it to break.
explanation.walkthrough: LENS reversed is SNEL, which takes HRAP after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is fragments of a bomb or shell thrown out by the explosion.

clue.text: Hack in trouble constantly

definitions.meaning: a hack is a worn-out horse
to keep finding fault, bothering someone repeatedly

explanation.surface: A journalist in constant difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a poor old horse, and to nag is to pester continually.

clue.text: Piece of bad luck in skirmish apparently

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Something unlucky seems to have happened in a skirmish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident.

clue.text: Record, one left by villain, lacking right conclusion

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the villain word is missing the right letter

parts.note: a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A record's one left-over villain lacks a righteous ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the concluding section of a book or play.
